title: Ines and the Alibi
premise: Hazel Joubert, the night concierge of the Hotel Verlaine, has spent fifteen years cataloguing the town's secrets in a private ledger—until a drowned woman washes up at the boathouse wearing clothes stolen from Hazel's own closet and carrying ID that reads 'Ines Joubert,' a sister Hazel buried decades ago. As Detective Amara Okafor closes in on Hazel as the obvious suspect, Hazel must decode their own ledger's hidden cipher to find who knew about Ines—and why someone wanted Hazel erased. The killer is the hotel's beloved owner, who murdered Ines fifteen years ago and has been waiting for Hazel to remember; the climax comes when Hazel trades the ledger for a confession recorded by the whole town at the Verlaine's centennial gala.
about_author: Oscar Fairweather is the pen name of a former hotel night manager who swears every front desk keeps two ledgers—one for guests, one for everyone else. He writes mysteries from a rented room above a shuttered grand hotel on the coast.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Checked Out
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. During a rain-soaked shift, Hazel finds the body at the boathouse—a woman in Hazel's own gray coat, wallet bearing the name Ines Joubert, the sister Hazel reported dead fifteen years ago. The emotional beat is vertigo: the invisible man suddenly visible, his carefully filed life turned inside out. Ends with Detective Okafor asking why the victim was dressed as him.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel and Okafor POVs. Under suspicion, Hazel rereads the ledger and discovers entries from fifteen years ago have been subtly altered—in their own handwriting they don't remember writing. Flashbacks reveal Ines worked at the Verlaine before her 'death.' The beat is dread deepening into self-doubt: if the ledger lies, so might Hazel's memory. Okafor finds the closet key missing from Hazel's ring.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Kept
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, racing the clock after an anonymous note promises 'the second Joubert dies at midnight.' Decoding the cipher hidden in room-assignment numbers, Hazel reconstructs the truth: owner Marguerite Voss killed Ines, who'd discovered Voss laundering money through the hotel, then gaslit young Hazel into believing he'd imagined it all. Climax at the centennial gala, where Hazel baits Voss publicly and records her confession over the ballroom speakers.

chapters.title: Checkout
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV closing into Hazel's. Voss is arrested; the town reckons with what its beloved hotel really was. Hazel hands Okafor the full ledger—an act of trust that costs him his invisibility but buys belonging. Final beat: Hazel checks himself into Room 9 as a guest for one night, signing the register under his own name for the first time in fifteen years, finally home.
